cases.query: For July through December 2025, which customer segments had the lowest repeat-purchase rate? Define repeat purchase using delivered orders and cite the order-history evidence.

required_claims: The segment-level repeat-purchase rates use customers with at least one delivered order in July through December 2025 as the denominator and customers with at least two delivered orders in that window as repeat purchasers.
Premium has 24 repeat customers among 68 active customers (35.29%) and Value has 54 among 153 (35.29%); these segments tie for the lowest rate.
Core has 99 repeat customers among 261 active customers (37.93%).
This is a descriptive segment comparison and does not establish why repeat purchasing differs.
required_caveats: Customer segment values are current customer-row values, not historical snapshots.
Repeat purchase is defined within the selected six-month window and is not lifetime returning status.
forbidden_claims: The segment comparison proves why customers repeat or stop purchasing.
Premium or Value customers have a lower lifetime returning rate based on this within-window result.

cases.query: Compare delivered net sales by sales channel for September and August 2025.
cases.gold_calculation_sql:
SELECT o.channel,
            SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2025-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-09-01' THEN oi.line_net_sales ELSE 0 END) AS august_sales,
            SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2025-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-10-01' THEN oi.line_net_sales ELSE 0 END) AS september_sales
          FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
          WHERE o.status='delivered' AND o.order_date >= '2025-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-10-01'
          GROUP BY o.channel ORDER BY o.channel

required_claims: Marketplace delivered net product sales changed from USD 6,485.98 in August 2025 to USD 4,357.30 in September 2025 (USD -2,128.68; -32.82%).
Retail Partner delivered net product sales changed from USD 598.36 in August 2025 to USD 508.70 in September 2025 (USD -89.66; -14.98%).
Web delivered net product sales changed from USD 11,234.29 in August 2025 to USD 6,142.18 in September 2025 (USD -5,092.11; -45.33%).
Across channels, delivered net product sales changed from USD 18,318.63 to USD 11,008.18, a change of USD -7,310.45 (-39.91%).
The three channel changes reconcile to the overall change; the observed breakdown is descriptive and does not establish a cause.
required_caveats: The measure is sum of order_items.line_net_sales for delivered orders, filtered by orders.order_date; shipping and later refunds are excluded.
The data is synthetic demo data and the comparison is descriptive, not causal.
forbidden_claims: A sales channel caused the decline without causal evidence.

cases.query: Rank product categories by gross profit for the second half of 2025.
cases.gold_calculation_sql:
SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.line_gross_profit), 2) AS gross_profit
          FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
          JOIN products p ON p.product_id=oi.product_id
          WHERE o.status='delivered' AND o.order_date >= '2025-07-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01'
          GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY gross_profit DESC, p.category

required_claims: Delivered gross profit in July–December 2025 totaled USD 55,275.54 across the five product categories.
Rank 1: Storage, USD 17,104.52 in delivered gross profit.
Rank 2: Decor, USD 10,782.16 in delivered gross profit.
Rank 3: Bedding, USD 9,666.75 in delivered gross profit.
Rank 4: Lighting, USD 9,025.16 in delivered gross profit.
Rank 5: Kitchen, USD 8,696.95 in delivered gross profit.
Storage ranked first and Kitchen ranked fifth by delivered gross profit.
This is a descriptive ranking; it does not explain why category gross profit differs.
required_caveats: Gross profit is sum of order_items.line_gross_profit for delivered orders from July 1 through December 31, 2025.
Gross profit is before returns, fulfillment, marketing, and overhead; categories are current product-row categories.
The data is synthetic demo data; the ranking is descriptive and does not establish a cause.
forbidden_claims: The category ranking proves the cause of the profit differences.

cases.query: Compare customer lifecycle behavior for July 2025, August 2025, and September 2025, including active customers, repeat rate, delivered orders per customer, and net sales per active customer by new versus returning status.

required_claims: The report compares July, August, and September 2025 using distinct active customers, repeat-customer rate, delivered orders per active customer, and net product sales per active customer.
All active customers were 106 in July (6.60% repeat), 109 in August (10.09% repeat), and 71 in September (1.41% repeat).
New/returning status is assigned using the month of customers.first_order_date in available records; it is not necessarily a customer's first-ever purchase.
The customer metrics are descriptive and do not establish why customer behavior changed.
required_caveats: Active customers have at least one delivered order in a month; repeat customers have at least two distinct delivered orders in that month.
Net product sales use order_items.line_net_sales and exclude shipping and later refunds.
The synthetic demo data's observed order dates end on 2025-12-31, which is not a source-completeness watermark.
forbidden_claims: The within-month repeat rate proves lifetime retention or explains why customer behavior changed.

cases.query: For customers first recorded in July 2025, August 2025, or September 2025, compare cohort retention from month 0 through month 3 where observable, and state the cohort definition and observation limits.

required_claims: Cohorts use the recorded month of customers.first_order_date and retention is a distinct customer with at least one delivered order in an offset month divided by cohort size.
The July 2025 cohort had 6 recorded customers; retention was 6/6 (100.00%) at M+0, 1/6 (16.67%) at M+1, and 2/6 (33.33%) at M+2.
The August 2025 cohort had 12 recorded customers; retention was 10/12 (83.33%) at M+0, 1/12 (8.33%) at M+1, and 1/12 (8.33%) at M+2.
The September 2025 cohort had 2 recorded customers; retention was 2/2 (100.00%) at M+0, 0/2 at M+1, and 0/2 at M+2.
Cohort comparisons are descriptive and do not establish why customers returned or stopped purchasing.
required_caveats: first_order_date is the first recorded date in the available data and does not prove a customer's first-ever purchase.
Recent observation periods may be incomplete because the source has no completeness watermark; month 0 can be below 100%.
The source is synthetic Cedar & Stone demo data.
forbidden_claims: Observed cohort retention proves a cause or a future retention outcome.

cases.query: Compare return rates by product category in September 2025 versus August 2025. Show returned units, sold units, and observed refund amounts, rank the largest rate increases, and state whether the comparison proves a cause.

required_claims: Returned-unit rate is returned units divided by delivered units in the order-month cohort; refund amounts are reported as observed values.
Bedding's rate rose from 1/57 (1.75%) in August to 1/32 (3.13%) in September, an increase of 1.38 percentage points.
Lighting's rate rose from 2/48 (4.17%) in August to 2/37 (5.41%) in September, an increase of 1.24 percentage points.
The report includes all five categories and their returned-unit numerators, sold-unit denominators, rates, and observed refund amounts.
The comparison shows association only and does not establish a cause.
required_caveats: Returns are grouped by the original order month, not return-processing month; later cohorts can have different maturation windows.
Category rates are descriptive and do not establish a cause.
The source is synthetic Cedar & Stone demo data.
forbidden_claims: A category's return rate caused a sales decline.

cases.query: Compare positive-stock inventory snapshot share by product category in September 2025 versus August 2025. Include positive and total snapshot counts and average on-hand units, and explain the coverage limits.

required_claims: Positive-stock snapshot share is snapshots with on-hand units greater than zero divided by observed snapshots.
Bedding, Decor, Lighting, and Storage each changed from 4/4 positive snapshots (100.00%) in August to 6/8 (75.00%) in September, a decrease of 25 percentage points.
Kitchen remained at 4/4 positive snapshots (100.00%) in both August and September.
The report gives the category snapshot numerators, denominators, and average on-hand units for both months.
Snapshot changes are descriptive associations and do not prove inventory caused a sales change.
required_caveats: Inventory snapshots are point-in-time records and do not establish continuous availability or measure lost demand.
Observed snapshot counts differ by month and category; interpret the shares with that coverage in mind.
The source is synthetic Cedar & Stone demo data.
forbidden_claims: The observed snapshot share proves that inventory caused lower sales.
